result.summary: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS. No coverage gap, no test file changed by this validator. EXECUTED (MIX_ENV=test, LOG_LEVEL=error to cover the CI-environment risk, per file group, one mix at a time under the mixlock): migration 9 + no_writer_scan 7 + tasks_route_classes 11 + roles_scoped_approvers 13 = 40 passed; scope_for_role 27 passed; f1_context 33 passed; tasks_scope_http 18 passed; tasks_scope_inv5_http 19 passed (137 of 137 green under LOG_LEVEL=error; the new tests assert only on error-level lines via capture_log level :error, one constant scope_set_failed line, no id refutation, so no new test depends on the log level; CI sets no LOG_LEVEL and config/runtime.exs defaults the test env to debug). Two files were also re-run unmutated after the mutants (25 passed). mix format --check-formatted over the 8 new tests, both support fixtures and the 3 edited route_scope tests: exit 0. No skip tag, TODO, FIXME, sleep, wall-clock call or secret in any new or changed test file. COVERAGE: every assigned AC (12, 13 a-e, d2, d3, 14, 15, 16, 17, 20, 23 walk), every SEC step-24 merge condition (T-F1 up/down/replay, T-F2 scan incl. insert_all and ten seeded writer forms, T-F3..T-F7, T-F15 mixed case and refusals, INV-5 on all seven routes with invalid and valid bodies for assign/reassign, AC 15 real concurrent revocation at context and router level with lock-multiset equality, AC 16 off/shadow byte identity, AC 14 list/assignee/NULL exclusion, f1 on without principal, {:nodes, []}) and the REVIEWER notes (audit rows never carry scope_node_id, T-F1 uses 20_261_019_200_001) maps to a green test with real assertions (spec table cross-read against the requirements.yaml AC text and the lib diff). FLAKE: requests are hand-built auth_context dispatches (no AuthPipeline, no api_tokens.last_used_at write), so the #2729 second-boundary shape is absent; headers and ids are sorted before comparison. obs1_ruling.ruling: DOC FIX. Do not change the code.
reasons: AC 16 requires off and shadow to be byte-identical with no F1 statement; extending resolve_principal_scope/2 (called on every claim) with the allowed node set would add a grants and node-tree read to the off path, or force a mode branch inside the single place that reads groups and roles.

As built the node set is computed once per request by ScopeGate.scope_set_for_role/3 (memoised per permission and role, zero statements when not on) and re-read inside the transaction by f1_recheck with fresh grants (AC 15); resolve_principal_scope/2 stays the single reader of groups and roles for the routing check, which is what the AC sentence protects, and a test pins its three keys and two statements.
Both gates (SEC step-24, REVIEWER step-25) accepted the build as functionally equivalent.
obs1_ruling.recommended_text: Tasks.resolve_principal_scope/2 stays the single place groups and roles are read for the routing-role check and is NOT extended; the allowed node set comes from ScopeGate.scope_set_for_role/3 and Scope.allowed_set_for_role/2.

result.m2_judgement: EQUIVALENT. Making ScopeResolver.task_scope return :tenant_wide for a NULL node changes allowed_for_role? only for a principal holding TASK_WORKER tenant-wide, and every such principal holds the route permission tenant-wide, so Scope.allowed?(principal, route_permission, :tenant_wide) exempts it first; a scoped principal is denied against :tenant_wide anyway. The strong form (M2b, f1_allowed? letting NULL through) is killed (2 of 45). Assign and reassign do not use f1_allowed?.
